query_text: how to bounce back from a layoff

messages.content: how to bounce back from a layoff

message.content:
A strong bounce-back from a layoff starts with **processing the loss**, then shifting quickly into a structured plan: **inventory your skills, activate your network, keep your routine steady, and keep building marketable skills**.[1][2][4][5]

- **Give yourself a short reset.** Take time to grieve, reflect, and manage the emotional impact before pushing hard into applications.[4][5]
- **Write a skills inventory.** List your biggest accomplishments, strengths, technical skills, soft skills, and recent certifications so you can explain your value clearly in interviews.[1][2]
- **Reach out to your network.** Contact former colleagues, mentors, alumni groups, professional associations, and recruiters with a brief, positive update about what you did and what you’re looking for next.[2][4][5]
- **Stay active with work-like momentum.** Volunteer, freelance, or take short-term projects to preserve routine, keep skills sharp, and expand your network.[1][2][5]
- **Upgrade your skills.** Use the gap to earn a credential, take an online course, or build expertise in an in-demand area.[1][2][5]
- **Protect your mental health.** Regular exercise, meditation, hobbies, structured days, and support from therapists or support groups can help stabilize you during the transition.[1][2][5]

If you want, I can also turn this into a **30-day layoff recovery plan** or help you draft a **post-layoff LinkedIn message**.
